steps.message:
Build an 8-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation titled "The Power of Vaccination: From Smallpox Eradication to COVID-19 in Record Time" for public health professionals and policy analysts. The tone should be data-forward, authoritative, and accessible.

The narrative arc begins with the accelerating pace of vaccine development over two centuries, moves through dramatic evidence of disease elimination and reduction in the US (including state-level measles data and the smallpox eradication story), explains the mechanism of herd immunity, then confronts remaining coverage gaps before closing with key takeaways and a call to action for global health systems.

For the "vaccine-timeline-acceleration" slide, use a horizontal bar chart showing the time span from pathogen identification to vaccine licensure for at least five diseases, with COVID-19's record timeline visually emphasized. For the "us-disease-elimination" slide, include a structured table comparing pre-vaccine annual case/death counts to current figures, clearly marking diseases with 100% reduction. The "measles-heatmap-states" slide should reference a heatmap-style visualization with annotated milestone years (1963, 1971, 1980). The "herd-immunity-mechanism" slide should include a simple diagram illustrating how population-level vaccination shields vulnerable individuals.

Do not fabricate data not found in source_brief.md. All statistics, percentages, and historical dates must be drawn directly from the provided brief.


## Data Sources

1. **Read `/app/benchmark/source_brief.md`**  for all the subject-matter text, data tables, statistics, and figure references you may use in the presentation.
2. **Read `/app/benchmark/task_input.json`**  for **structural requirements**: deck metadata (slide count, aspect ratio, audience, tone) and a per-slide outline (id, title, objective) that your presentation must follow.

## Output Requirements

Save the final PPT to `/app/output/final_deck.pptx`.

Only the correctly saved final file is needed — no additional explanation is required.

---

## Automated Execution Rules

There is no human operator online for this session. Follow these rules:

1. **Skip all confirmation/approval/user-input steps** — do not pause, ask questions, or wait for a reply. When encountering BLOCKING or "wait for user confirmation" instructions, make a professional judgment and proceed.
2. **Design decisions** — if `task_input.json` specifies fields such as `deck.tone` or `deck.audience`, use them to guide template, color palette, and style choices; otherwise, use your professional judgment.
3. **Do not deploy or share** — no deployment, PDF export, share links, or other post-delivery steps are needed.
4. **Priority** — these rules take precedence over any interactive-wait instructions in SKILL.md. The workflow, quality standards, and technical specifications in SKILL.md remain in effect; only interactive waits are skipped.

1	# The Power of Vaccination: History, Impact, and Remaining Challenges
2	
3	## Source
4	https://ourworldindata.org/vaccination
5	
6	## History of Vaccine Development
7	
8	The first vaccine was created by Edward Jenner in 1796 against smallpox, using cowpox to trigger immunity. It took nearly a century before the next vaccine (rabies) was developed, because scientists didn't yet understand germ theory. Once Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch established germ theory in the late 19th century, vaccines for rabies, cholera, and anthrax followed.
9	
10	The timeline from pathogen identification to vaccine licensure has shortened dramatically over the past 140 years:
11	
12	| Disease | Pathogen Identified | Vaccine Licensed | Gap (Years) |
13	|---|---|---|---|
14	| Typhoid fever | 1884 | 1989 | 105 |
15	| Meningitis | 1889 | 1981 | 92 |
16	| Whooping cough | 1906 | 1948 | 42 |
17	| Polio | 1908 | 1955 | 47 |
18	| Measles | 1953 | 1963 | 10 |
19	| Chickenpox | 1953 | 1995 | 42 |
20	| Hepatitis B | 1965 | 1981 | 16 |
21	| Ebola | 1976 | 2019 | 43 |
22	| COVID-19 | 2020 | 2020 | <1 |
23	
24	![Vaccination innovation timeline from 1880 to 2020](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
25	
26	Modern tools — advanced microscopy, genome sequencing, mRNA technology, and virus-like particles — have enabled faster and more precise vaccine design.
27	
28	## Dramatic Disease Reductions in the United States
29	
30	Data from Roush and Murphy (2007) shows the reduction in cases and deaths for vaccine-preventable diseases in the US after vaccine introduction. Several diseases achieved 100% elimination of both cases and deaths.
31	
32	| Disease | Pre-Vaccine Cases (per million/yr) | Post-Vaccine Cases (per million/yr) | Case Reduction | Pre-Vaccine Deaths (per million/yr) | Death Reduction |
33	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
34	| Diphtheria | 158 | 0 | 100% | 13.7 | 100% |
35	| Measles | 3,044 | 0.2 | 99.99% | 2.5 | 100% |
36	| Smallpox | 250 | 0 | 100% | 2.9 | 100% |
37	| Acute polio | 141 | 0 | 100% | 10 | 100% |
38	| Pertussis | 1,534 | 52 | 96.6% | 30.8 | 99.7% |
39	| Rubella | 242 | 0.04 | 99.98% | 0.09 | 100% |
40	| Hepatitis A | 465 | 51 | 89% | 0.5 | 88.7% |
41	| Acute hepatitis B | 273 | 44 | 83.9% | 1 | 83.6% |
42	| Pneumococcal | 233 | 139 | 40.5% | 24 | 31.3% |
43	
44	![US vaccine-preventable disease reductions](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
45	
46	## Measles Elimination Across US States
47	
48	A heatmap of measles cases per 100,000 across all 50 US states from 1929 to 2022 shows the dramatic impact of vaccination. Three key milestones transformed the landscape:
49	
50	- **1963**: First measles vaccine developed by John Enders
51	- **1971**: MMR (measles-mumps-rubella) vaccine developed by Maurice Hilleman
52	- **1980**: Vaccination became mandatory for children entering kindergarten
53	
54	Before 1963, nearly every state experienced high measles incidence (100–1,000+ cases per 100,000). After the 1980 mandate, cases dropped to near zero across all states, with only sporadic outbreaks.
55	
56	![Measles heatmap across US states](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
57	
58	## Smallpox Eradication: The Greatest Vaccination Success
59	
60	Smallpox was declared eradicated worldwide in 1980 — the only human disease to be fully eliminated through vaccination. Key factors enabling eradication: the virus infected only humans, symptoms were distinguishable, and the vaccine was cheap and effective. The WHO passed a resolution to eradicate smallpox in 1959, launched an intensified campaign in 1967, and the last natural case occurred in Somalia in 1977.
61	
62	## Herd Immunity and Remaining Challenges
63	
64	Vaccines protect not only individuals but entire communities through herd immunity. When enough people are vaccinated, pathogens cannot spread effectively, shielding those who cannot be vaccinated — newborns, immunocompromised individuals, and cancer patients on chemotherapy.
65	
66	However, significant challenges remain. Pneumococcal disease has seen only a 40.5% reduction in cases and 31.3% in deaths. Hepatitis A and B still show incomplete control. Globally, not everyone has access to vaccines, supply shortages put children at risk, and poor scientific understanding can reduce trust and uptake.
67	
68	## Key Findings
69	
70	- **Vaccines achieved 100% elimination** of cases and deaths for diphtheria, smallpox, and both forms of polio in the US.
71	- **Vaccine development timelines have collapsed** from over 100 years (typhoid) to under 1 year (COVID-19), driven by mRNA technology and genomic tools.
72	- **Measles cases dropped to near zero** across all 50 US states following the 1980 kindergarten vaccination mandate.
73	- **Smallpox remains the only human disease eradicated** through vaccination, certified in 1980 after a global campaign.
74	- **Gaps persist** for pneumococcal disease (40.5% case reduction), hepatitis A (89%), and hepatitis B (83.9%), highlighting the need for improved access, coverage, and newer vaccines.

Data from Roush and Murphy (2007) shows the reduction in cases and deaths for vaccine-preventable diseases in the US after vaccine introduction. Several diseases achieved 100% elimination of both cases and deaths.

def add_slide(prs, layout_idx=6):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[layout_idx]
    return prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

def solid_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    fill = slide.background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", italic=False, wrap=True):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.name = font_name
    return txBox

def add_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        1,  # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE
        left, top, width, height
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def slide_header(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=None):
    """Add a navy header bar with title."""
    bar = add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, Inches(1.15), NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.15), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.75),
                title_text, font_size=28, bold=True, color=WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    if subtitle_text:
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.82), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.38),
                    subtitle_text, font_size=14, bold=False, color=LIGHTGRAY,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

def embed_figure(slide, img_path, left, top, width, height):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, left, top, width, height)

def fig_to_png(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf

def build_herd_immunity_slide(prs):
    """Herd immunity mechanism diagram."""
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    solid_bg(slide, WHITE)
    slide_header(slide,
                 "Herd Immunity: How Vaccinating Many Protects the Most Vulnerable",
                 "Population-level vaccination shields those who cannot be vaccinated")

    # Build diagram with matplotlib
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 4.6))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")

    def draw_population(ax, title, vacc_fraction, spread_active):
        ax.set_facecolor("#F8F9FC")
        ax.set_xlim(0, 10)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 6)
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color="#0D2B5C", pad=8)

        np.random.seed(42)
        n = 30
        xs = np.random.uniform(0.5, 9.5, n)
        ys = np.random.uniform(0.5, 5.5, n)

        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(xs, ys)):
            is_vacc = i < int(n * vacc_fraction)
            is_vuln = i == int(n * 0.5)   # one 'vulnerable' individual
            is_infected = (not is_vacc) and spread_active and (i > int(n * vacc_fraction) + 1)

            if is_vuln:
                color = "#D62B2B"
                marker = "s"
                ms = 12
            elif is_vacc:
                color = "#00878A"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            elif is_infected and spread_active:
                color = "#F0A500"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            else:
                color = "#AABBCC"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            ax.plot(x, y, marker, color=color, markersize=ms,
                    markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.8)

        # Shield symbol around vulnerable node when herd immunity
        if vacc_fraction >= 0.8:
            vx, vy = xs[int(n * 0.5)], ys[int(n * 0.5)]
            shield = plt.Circle((vx, vy), 0.55, color="#00878A", alpha=0.25, zorder=0)
            ax.add_patch(shield)
            ax.plot(vx, vy, "o", color="#D62B2B", markersize=12,
                    markeredgecolor="#00878A", markeredgewidth=2.5)

    draw_population(axes[0], "Low Vaccination Coverage\n(pathogen spreads freely)",
                    vacc_fraction=0.3, spread_active=True)
    draw_population(axes[1], "High Vaccination Coverage\n(herd immunity achieved)",
                    vacc_fraction=0.85, spread_active=False)

    # Legend
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    legend_elements = [
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor="#00878A",
               markersize=10, label="Vaccinated individual"),
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="s", color="w", markerfacecolor="#D62B2B",
               markersize=10, label="Vulnerable (cannot be vaccinated)"),
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor="#F0A500",
               markersize=10, label="Infected / spreading disease"),
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor="#AABBCC",
               markersize=10, label="Unvaccinated (susceptible)"),
    ]
    fig.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="lower center", ncol=4,
               fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))

    plt.tight_layout(pad=0.5)
    png = fig_to_png(fig)
    plt.close(fig)

    slide.shapes.add_picture(png, Inches(0.25), Inches(1.2),
                              Inches(10.5), Inches(5.5))

    # Side callout
    add_rect(slide, Inches(10.9), Inches(1.3), Inches(2.25), Inches(4.8), NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(11.0), Inches(1.4), Inches(2.1), Inches(4.6),
                "Vaccines protect:\n\n• Newborns\n\n• Immunocompromised patients\n\n• Cancer patients on chemotherapy\n\nwho cannot receive vaccines themselves.",
                font_size=11, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.25), Inches(6.95), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.35),

"""Build final_deck.pptx for The Power of Vaccination presentation."""

import io
import os
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.chart.data import ChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker

# ── Palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
NAVY      = RGBColor(0x0D, 0x2B, 0x5C)   # dark navy – headers / accents
TEAL      = RGBColor(0x00, 0x87, 0x8A)   # teal – highlight bars / callouts
GOLD      = RGBColor(0xF0, 0xA5, 0x00)   # gold – COVID-19 / emphasis
WHITE     = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHTGRAY = RGBColor(0xF2, 0xF4, 0xF7)
DARKGRAY  = RGBColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x44)
RED_EM    = RGBColor(0xD6, 0x2B, 0x2B)

SLIDE_W = Inches(13.33)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)

ASSETS = "/app/benchmark/assets"


# ── Helper utilities ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def add_slide(prs, layout_idx=6):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[layout_idx]
    return prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

def solid_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    fill = slide.background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", italic=False, wrap=True):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.name = font_name
    return txBox

def add_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        1,  # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE
        left, top, width, height
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def slide_header(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=None):
    """Add a navy header bar with title."""
    bar = add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, Inches(1.15), NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.15), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.75),
                title_text, font_size=28, bold=True, color=WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    if subtitle_text:
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.82), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.38),
                    subtitle_text, font_size=14, bold=False, color=LIGHTGRAY,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

def embed_figure(slide, img_path, left, top, width, height):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, left, top, width, height)

def fig_to_png(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf


# ── Slide builders ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def build_title_slide(prs):
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    solid_bg(slide, NAVY)

    # Teal accent bar on left

                font_size=24, bold=False, color=GOLD, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    # Divider line
    from pptx.util import Pt as UPt
    line = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, Inches(0.55), Inches(4.25),
                                   Inches(11.5), Pt(2))
    line.fill.solid()
    line.fill.fore_color.rgb = TEAL
    line.line.fill.background()

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(4.5), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
                "Scope: 1796 – 2020  |  A two-century journey of scientific innovation and global health impact",

    slide.shapes.add_picture(png, Inches(0.25), Inches(1.25),
                              Inches(9.6), Inches(5.7))

    # Callout box
    cb = add_rect(slide, Inches(10.05), Inches(1.35), Inches(3.1), Inches(2.2),
                  NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(10.15), Inches(1.45), Inches(2.9), Inches(2.0),
                "mRNA technology, genome sequencing & advanced microscopy collapsed development timelines from over a century to under a year.",
                font_size=12, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    cb2 = add_rect(slide, Inches(10.05), Inches(3.75), Inches(3.1), Inches(1.2),

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(10.12), Inches(3.82), Inches(2.9), Inches(1.05),

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.25), Inches(6.95), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.35),

def build_us_disease_slide(prs):

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 4.6))

        ax.set_ylim(0, 6)

        ys = np.random.uniform(0.5, 5.5, n)

        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(xs, ys)):
            is_vacc = i < int(n * vacc_fraction)
            is_vuln = i == int(n * 0.5)   # one 'vulnerable' individual
            is_infected = (not is_vacc) and spread_active and (i > int(n * vacc_fraction) + 1)

            if is_vuln:
                color = "#D62B2B"
                marker = "s"
                ms = 12
            elif is_vacc:
                color = "#00878A"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            elif is_infected and spread_active:
                color = "#F0A500"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            else:

                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            ax.plot(x, y, marker, color=color, markersize=ms,
                    markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.8)

            vx, vy = xs[int(n * 0.5)], ys[int(n * 0.5)]

"""Build final_deck.pptx for The Power of Vaccination presentation."""

import io
import os
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu

from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
from pptx.chart.data import ChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker

# ── Palette ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
NAVY      = RGBColor(0x0D, 0x2B, 0x5C)   # dark navy – headers / accents
TEAL      = RGBColor(0x00, 0x87, 0x8A)   # teal – highlight bars / callouts
GOLD      = RGBColor(0xF0, 0xA5, 0x00)   # gold – COVID-19 / emphasis
WHITE     = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHTGRAY = RGBColor(0xF2, 0xF4, 0xF7)
DARKGRAY  = RGBColor(0x33, 0x33, 0x44)
RED_EM    = RGBColor(0xD6, 0x2B, 0x2B)

SLIDE_W = Inches(13.33)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)

ASSETS = "/app/benchmark/assets"


# ── Helper utilities ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def add_slide(prs, layout_idx=6):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[layout_idx]
    return prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

def solid_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    fill = slide.background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", italic=False, wrap=True):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.name = font_name
    return txBox

def add_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        1,  # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE
        left, top, width, height
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def slide_header(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=None):
    """Add a navy header bar with title."""
    bar = add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, Inches(1.15), NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.15), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.75),
                title_text, font_size=28, bold=True, color=WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    if subtitle_text:
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.82), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.38),
                    subtitle_text, font_size=14, bold=False, color=LIGHTGRAY,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

def embed_figure(slide, img_path, left, top, width, height):

def fig_to_png(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf


# ── Slide builders ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

def build_title_slide(prs):

                font_size=24, bold=False, color=GOLD, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    line = slide.shapes.add_shape(1, Inches(0.55), Inches(4.25),
                                   Inches(11.5), Pt(2))
    line.fill.solid()
    line.fill.fore_color.rgb = TEAL
    line.line.fill.background()

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(4.5), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
                "Scope: 1796 – 2020  |  A two-century journey of scientific innovation and global health impact",
                font_size=14, color=LIGHTGRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.55), Inches(6.5), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.45),

    diseases = [

        ys = np.random.uniform(0.5, 5.5, n)

        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(xs, ys)):
            is_vacc = i < int(n * vacc_fraction)
            is_vuln = i == int(n * 0.5)   # one 'vulnerable' individual
            is_infected = (not is_vacc) and spread_active and (i > int(n * vacc_fraction) + 1)

                color = "#D62B2B"
                marker = "s"
                ms = 12

                marker = "o"

                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            else:

                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            ax.plot(x, y, marker, color=color, markersize=ms,
                    markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.8)

def add_slide(prs, layout_idx=6):
    layout = prs.slide_layouts[layout_idx]
    return prs.slides.add_slide(layout)

def solid_bg(slide, color: RGBColor):
    fill = slide.background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                bold=False, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                font_name="Calibri", italic=False, wrap=True):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = wrap
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.alignment = align
    run = p.add_run()
    run.text = text
    run.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    run.font.bold = bold
    run.font.italic = italic
    run.font.color.rgb = color
    run.font.name = font_name
    return txBox

def add_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color, line_color=None):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        1,  # MSO_SHAPE_TYPE.RECTANGLE
        left, top, width, height
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    if line_color:
        shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    else:
        shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape

def slide_header(slide, title_text, subtitle_text=None):
    """Add a navy header bar with title."""
    bar = add_rect(slide, 0, 0, SLIDE_W, Inches(1.15), NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.15), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.75),
                title_text, font_size=28, bold=True, color=WHITE,
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
    if subtitle_text:
        add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.35), Inches(0.82), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.38),
                    subtitle_text, font_size=14, bold=False, color=LIGHTGRAY,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

def embed_figure(slide, img_path, left, top, width, height):
    slide.shapes.add_picture(img_path, left, top, width, height)

def fig_to_png(fig):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(buf, format="png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
    buf.seek(0)
    return buf

        ("Smallpox",        "250",   "0",    "100% ✓", "2.9",   "100% ✓"),

        ("Measles",         "3,044", "0.2",  "99.99% ✓","2.5",  "100% ✓"),

        ("Hepatitis A",     "465",   "51",   "89%",    "0.5",   "88.7%"),
        ("Acute Hep. B",    "273",   "44",   "83.9%",  "1",     "83.6%"),
        ("Pneumococcal",    "233",   "139",  "40.5% !", "24",   "31.3% !"),
    ]

    col_widths = [Inches(1.85), Inches(1.45), Inches(1.45),
                  Inches(1.3),  Inches(1.45), Inches(1.3)]
    total_w = sum(col_widths)
    left_start = Inches(0.35)
    top_start  = Inches(1.25)
    row_h      = Inches(0.44)

    def cell_rect(r, c, w, h):
        l = left_start + sum(col_widths[:c])
        t = top_start + r * row_h
        return l, t, w, h

    def cell_text(slide, r, c, text, bg, fg=DARKGRAY, bold=False, sz=10):
        l, t, w, h = cell_rect(r, c, col_widths[c], row_h)
        rect = add_rect(slide, l, t, w, h, bg,
                        line_color=RGBColor(0xDD, 0xDD, 0xE8))

                    w - Inches(0.08), h - Inches(0.04),
                    text, font_size=sz, bold=bold, color=fg,
                    align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

    # Header row
    for ci, hdr in enumerate(headers):
        cell_text(slide, 0, ci, hdr, NAVY, WHITE, bold=True, sz=10)

    # Data rows
    for ri, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):
        # alternating background
        alt = LIGHTGRAY if ri % 2 == 0 else WHITE
        for ci, val in enumerate(row):
            bg = alt
            fg = DARKGRAY
            bold = False
            # 100% reductions → green tint

                bg = RGBColor(0xD4, 0xED, 0xDA)
                fg = RGBColor(0x15, 0x55, 0x24)
                bold = True
            # remaining burden → orange tint

                bg = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xF3, 0xCD)
                fg = RGBColor(0x85, 0x56, 0x04)
                bold = True
            cell_text(slide, ri, ci, val, bg, fg, bold=bold)

                "! = Incomplete control — remaining burden", font_size=10,
                color=DARKGRAY)

def build_herd_immunity_slide(prs):
    """Herd immunity mechanism diagram."""
    slide = add_slide(prs)
    solid_bg(slide, WHITE)
    slide_header(slide,
                 "Herd Immunity: How Vaccinating Many Protects the Most Vulnerable",
                 "Population-level vaccination shields those who cannot be vaccinated")

    # Build diagram with matplotlib
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.5, 4.6))
    fig.patch.set_facecolor("white")

    def draw_population(ax, title, vacc_fraction, spread_active):
        ax.set_facecolor("#F8F9FC")
        ax.set_xlim(0, 10)
        ax.set_ylim(0, 6)
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        ax.axis("off")
        ax.set_title(title, fontsize=12, fontweight="bold", color="#0D2B5C", pad=8)

        np.random.seed(42)
        n = 30
        xs = np.random.uniform(0.5, 9.5, n)
        ys = np.random.uniform(0.5, 5.5, n)

        for i, (x, y) in enumerate(zip(xs, ys)):
            is_vacc = i < int(n * vacc_fraction)
            is_vuln = i == int(n * 0.5)   # one 'vulnerable' individual
            is_infected = (not is_vacc) and spread_active and (i > int(n * vacc_fraction) + 1)

            if is_vuln:
                color = "#D62B2B"
                marker = "s"
                ms = 12
            elif is_vacc:
                color = "#00878A"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            elif is_infected and spread_active:
                color = "#F0A500"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            else:
                color = "#AABBCC"
                marker = "o"
                ms = 10
            ax.plot(x, y, marker, color=color, markersize=ms,
                    markeredgecolor="white", markeredgewidth=0.8)

        # Shield symbol around vulnerable node when herd immunity
        if vacc_fraction >= 0.8:
            vx, vy = xs[int(n * 0.5)], ys[int(n * 0.5)]
            shield = plt.Circle((vx, vy), 0.55, color="#00878A", alpha=0.25, zorder=0)
            ax.add_patch(shield)
            ax.plot(vx, vy, "o", color="#D62B2B", markersize=12,
                    markeredgecolor="#00878A", markeredgewidth=2.5)

    draw_population(axes[0], "Low Vaccination Coverage\n(pathogen spreads freely)",
                    vacc_fraction=0.3, spread_active=True)
    draw_population(axes[1], "High Vaccination Coverage\n(herd immunity achieved)",
                    vacc_fraction=0.85, spread_active=False)

    # Legend
    from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
    legend_elements = [
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor="#00878A",
               markersize=10, label="Vaccinated individual"),
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="s", color="w", markerfacecolor="#D62B2B",
               markersize=10, label="Vulnerable (cannot be vaccinated)"),
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor="#F0A500",
               markersize=10, label="Infected / spreading disease"),
        Line2D([0], [0], marker="o", color="w", markerfacecolor="#AABBCC",
               markersize=10, label="Unvaccinated (susceptible)"),
    ]
    fig.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc="lower center", ncol=4,
               fontsize=9, framealpha=0.9, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.01))

    plt.tight_layout(pad=0.5)
    png = fig_to_png(fig)
    plt.close(fig)

    slide.shapes.add_picture(png, Inches(0.25), Inches(1.2),
                              Inches(10.5), Inches(5.5))

    # Side callout
    add_rect(slide, Inches(10.9), Inches(1.3), Inches(2.25), Inches(4.8), NAVY)
    add_textbox(slide, Inches(11.0), Inches(1.4), Inches(2.1), Inches(4.6),
                "Vaccines protect:\n\n• Newborns\n\n• Immunocompromised patients\n\n• Cancer patients on chemotherapy\n\nwho cannot receive vaccines themselves.",
                font_size=11, color=WHITE, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

    add_textbox(slide, Inches(0.25), Inches(6.95), Inches(12.5), Inches(0.35),
                "Source: Our World in Data – ourworldindata.org/vaccination",
                font_size=9, color=DARKGRAY, italic=True)
